recipe_version.title: Skillet Shakshuka
recipe_version.description: Eggs set in a skillet of tomato and red pepper sauce made from crushed tomatoes, peppers, onion, and ground spices.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: 8 large eggs, 2 per serving. Counted whole eggs only.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: all of it for the onion and peppers

ingredients.name: canned crushed tomatoes
ingredients.note: one 28 oz can. Store-bought crushed tomatoes. Not a jar of shakshuka sauce.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: all of it goes into the sauce

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: divided: 1/4 tsp with the onion and peppers, 3/4 tsp in the sauce, 1/4 tsp on the eggs

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.note: all of it in the sauce

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Dice the yellow onion. Stem, seed, and slice the red bell pepper. Mince the garlic. Chop the fresh parsley. Measure the sweet paprika, ground cumin, ground coriander, sugar, kosher salt, and black pepper. Leave the eggs whole until the sauce can hold a well.

steps.title: Soften the onion and peppers
steps.body: Heat the olive oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the yellow onion, the red bell pepper, and 1/4 tsp of the kosher salt. Cook, stirring, until the onion is soft and the pepper has slumped, about 8 minutes. Do not char them.

steps.title: Bloom the spices
steps.body: Add the garlic, sweet paprika, ground cumin, and ground coriander. Stir for 1 minute, until fragrant. These are ground spices, not a jar of shakshuka sauce and not a paste.

steps.title: Simmer the tomato-pepper sauce
steps.body: Pour in the canned crushed tomatoes and the water. Add the sugar, 3/4 tsp of the kosher salt, and the black pepper. Stir. Simmer uncovered over medium heat until the sauce thickens enough that a spoon leaves a well, about 10 minutes. This tomato-pepper sauce is the only sauce, and it is made in this skillet. Do not add cheese, yogurt, butter, cream, or bread.

steps.title: Set the eggs
steps.body: Make 8 wells in the sauce. Crack 1 egg into each well, 8 eggs total, 2 per serving. Sprinkle the remaining 1/4 tsp kosher salt over the eggs. Cover the skillet. Cook over medium-low for 6 to 8 minutes. The whites must be fully set, with no liquid white at the edge. The yolks stay soft and glossy. Do not flip the eggs. For firm yolks, cover about 2 minutes more. The written target is soft yolks. kitchen_tested is false.

steps.title: Finish in the skillet
steps.body: Take the skillet off the heat. Scatter the fresh parsley over the sauce and eggs. Serve from the skillet. Each serving is 2 eggs with tomato-pepper sauce. No cheese, no yogurt, no bread, and no second sauce.

recipe_version.heat: Medium for the onion, peppers, and sauce. Medium-low, covered, for the eggs. No oven.
recipe_version.doneness: Sauce holds a well after about 10 minutes of simmering. Eggs: whites fully set, no liquid white, yolks soft and glossy. Do not flip them. Firm yolks need about 2 extra covered minutes and are not the written target. kitchen_tested is false.

curator_preflight.detail: Every listed ingredient is used in a step. Parsley is scattered at the end. No cheese, bread, or yogurt is introduced in the method.
Olive oil is 2 tbsp and it is all used to soften the onion and peppers.

The tomato-pepper sauce is simmered in the skillet from canned crushed tomatoes, red bell pepper, onion, garlic, paprika, cumin, coriander, water, sugar, salt, and pepper. It is not a jar of shakshuka sauce.
Prep 12 (cutting and measuring) + cook 26 (8 onion and pepper + 1 spices + 10 sauce + 7 eggs) = 38. No oven preheat. The egg range is 6 to 8 minutes; the clock uses 7.
Base 4. Eggs scale as whole eggs: 2, 4, and 8. A 28 oz can does not quarter by shopping unit. See scaling_notes.

scaling_notes.1: Two large eggs, not a fraction of an egg. Use an 8-inch skillet so the sauce is deep enough for wells. Tomato floor: 7 oz canned crushed tomatoes (about 3/4 cup), not an empty quarter of a can with no sauce left. Onion floor: 1/2 small yellow onion, not a few dice. Pepper: 1/2 red bell pepper. Garlic: 1 clove, not a quarter clove. Oil: 2 tsp. Water: 2 tbsp. Spices: 1/2 tsp sweet paprika, 1/4 tsp ground cumin, 1/4 tsp ground coriander. Sugar: 1/4 tsp. Salt: a pinch on the vegetables, 1/4 tsp in the sauce, a pinch on the eggs. Parsley: 1 tbsp chopped. Simmer the sauce at least 6 minutes so it can hold a well. Egg time stays 6 to 8 minutes covered. Same medium then medium-low heat.
scaling_notes.2: Four large eggs in a 10-inch skillet. Half the can of crushed tomatoes (14 oz). One red bell pepper, 1/2 yellow onion, 2 garlic cloves. Halve the oil, water, sugar, salt, parsley, and spices. Same heat and the same 6 to 8 minute egg target.
scaling_notes.4: As written. Eight large eggs, two per person, in a 12-inch skillet. One 28 oz can of crushed tomatoes.
do_not_scale: skillet size must shrink with the batch so the wells stay in sauce

coverage_contribution: Puts eggs on the dinner plate as the protein, in a skillet of sauce, which the live 24 and the seven certified drafts do not do. HH001 can eat eggs. The tomato-pepper sauce is built in the pan. North African is already a live cuisine label; the new cell is eggs plus this skillet format.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with Moroccan Chickpea Skillet: both are saucy skillets, but that meal is chickpeas under a different cuisine slug and has no eggs. Compared with Harissa Roasted Carrots with Feta: same north-african label already in the live catalog, but that one is roasted carrots and dairy. This skillet has no dairy. Compared with the Dry Run #1 chicken sandwich draft: that draft uses egg as a coating for poultry and bread, which HH001 cannot eat. These eggs are the dinner, with no bread and no poultry. Not a bowl, taco, or pasta.
